headline: Pyridostigmine
punch: It doubled the GH response to exercise.

headline: What it actually is
body: An old, cheap, orally active cholinesterase inhibitor, licensed for myasthenia gravis. It stops acetylcholine being broken down, so cholinergic tone rises. | Cholinergic tone is one of the inputs that lowers **hypothalamic somatostatin**, and somatostatin is the brake gating every other input to GH. That is why this unremarkable drug became a standard research probe of the GH axis.
punch: It does not push GH. It releases the brake.

headline: It doubles exercise GH
body: Nine healthy volunteers, measured both ways. Exercise alone gave a GH area under the curve of **292.6**. The same exercise after pyridostigmine gave **587.3**, P < 0.005. | Peak GH went from 6.5 to **13.5 µg/l**, P < 0.01. Same session, same people, roughly double the growth hormone, purely from easing the brake beforehand.

headline: It is additive
body: The authors did the arithmetic most studies skip. The effect was **additive** to exercise, because the sum of the two separate responses was not significantly different from the combined one. | That is useful to know when reasoning about stacking: it behaves as an independent second input arriving alongside the first, not as a multiplier on it.
punch: Two inputs stacking. Not one amplifying the other.

headline: It enhances the first pulse
subhead: BENEFIT · AND THIS IS THE CATCH
body: Spoudeas gave two GHRH stimuli 90 minutes apart on a pyridostigmine background. It **enhanced the first GH response** with an increased release rate. | This is the finding that should shape how anyone uses it, and almost nobody quotes it.
punch: It works where you time it.

headline: The second pulse gets nothing
body: In that same experiment, the **second GH responses were not augmented**. Same background, same session, 90 minutes later, and the benefit was gone. | So dosing it repeatedly through the day is not purchasing repeated benefit. It opens one window. What you put in that window is the decision, not how many times you dose.

headline: It does not rescue an axis
body: Marcell ran it in young and old men. It raised GH during maximal exercise, **20.9 against 4.9**, and submaximal, **12.3 against 4.7**, both P < 0.05. Large and real in both groups. | But it **failed to restore the responses of the old to those of the young**, and the authors concluded raised somatostatin does not completely explain the age difference. Lifting the brake does not rebuild the engine.
punch: It lifts the brake. Something else is still wrong.

headline: Cholinergic side effects
body: It is a cholinesterase inhibitor, so the predictable effects are cholinergic: gastrointestinal cramping, increased secretions, sweating, and at higher doses muscle fasciculation. | These are dose-related and they are the reason the research protocols use modest oral doses rather than pushing it. The GH studies above used **30 and 60 mg** orally.
punch: The side effects are the mechanism, working elsewhere.

headline: Time it to one window
body: If it only improves the pulse it is timed to, then the entire mitigation is placement rather than frequency. One dose, anchored to the pulse that matters most to you. | Around **70%** of daily GH comes out in early sleep when somatostatin has already withdrawn, which is the window where the brake is lowest to begin with.

headline: There are other doors
body: Cholinergic tone is one route to the same gate, not the only one. **Arginine lowers somatostatin tone** and potentiates the GHRH response, which is exactly why the arginine plus GHRH test is a standard human probe of GH reserve. | So if cholinergic side effects are the limiting factor, the gate itself is still reachable by a different and much better-tolerated route.
punch: The gate has more than one door.

headline: It is a probe, not a protocol
body: Every human study quoted here uses pyridostigmine as a **research probe**, to measure how much somatostatin is currently holding GH down in a given person. That is what the pyridostigmine test is for. | It has not been studied as a growth protocol, there is no height endpoint anywhere in this literature, and the distance between an established mechanism and a tested application is the entire gap.

headline: Verdict
body: The best-evidenced somatostatin lever available, in humans, at an oral dose, with a doubling of exercise GH measured directly. Cheap, old, and well characterised. | Its limit is sharp and specific: one window per dose, no benefit to the second pulse, no rescue of a blunted axis, and no outcome trial. Treat it as a timing tool rather than a daily compound.
punch: A real lever with one window per pull.
